topics.title: Why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
topics.catch: Binary floats can't store 0.1 exactly, so tiny errors appear
topics.verdict: Never compare floats with ==; use integers (cents) or a decimal type for money
topics.demand_evidence: own judgment: classic question, no demand data behind it

topics.title: Cache stampede: when one expired key kills your database
topics.hook: One hot key expires and a thousand requests hit the DB at once
topics.catch: Every request misses together and the DB falls over
topics.verdict: Lock so one request rebuilds, or refresh early before expiry (TTL jitter dropped: Wikipedia does not cover it)
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #18 (caching)

topics.title: Idempotency keys: how a retry doesn't charge you twice
topics.hook: Network times out, client retries, customer charged twice
topics.catch: Retries are unsafe for non-idempotent writes
topics.verdict: Client sends a unique key; server stores the first result and replays it
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #1 and #4 (idempotency)
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T03.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Why is my SQL query slow? (indexes)
topics.hook: Same query: scans a million rows vs jumps straight to one
topics.catch: An index speeds reads but slows writes and takes space
topics.verdict: Index columns you filter and join on; check with EXPLAIN
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #5 (slow SQL)
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T04.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: JWT vs session cookie: where does login state live?
topics.hook: Server remembers you vs you carry a signed token
topics.catch: A JWT can't be easily revoked before it expires
topics.verdict: Short expiry plus refresh, or server sessions when you need instant logout
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #12 (auth/JWT)
topics.source_to_verify: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519 ; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T05.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: CAP theorem in plain English
topics.hook: Network splits: do you answer possibly stale, or refuse?
topics.catch: During a partition you must pick consistency or availability
topics.verdict: Choose per feature (payments vs likes), not per company
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #6 and #24; DesignGurus 'most frequently asked system design questions' (consistency)
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T06.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Sync API vs message queue: when to wait and when not to
topics.hook: User waits 30 s for an email vs gets instant OK and email arrives later
topics.catch: Queues add delay, ordering and duplicate-delivery issues
topics.verdict: Queue slow, non-urgent work; keep the answer-now path synchronous
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #19
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T07.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: The N+1 query problem
topics.hook: One page load fires 101 queries instead of 2
topics.catch: Lazy loading hides a query per row in a loop
topics.verdict: Join or prefetch (eager load) and watch query counts
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #5 (adjacent: slow queries)
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T08.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: CORS: why your browser blocks your own API
topics.hook: Request works in Postman, fails in the browser
topics.catch: CORS is browser-enforced, not a server security feature
topics.verdict: Server sends the right Access-Control headers; never use * with credentials
topics.demand_evidence: own judgment: classic question, no demand data behind it

topics.title: Rate limiting with a token bucket
topics.hook: One client sends a flood and everyone slows down
topics.catch: Bursts and per-instance counters make limits uneven
topics.verdict: Refill tokens at a steady rate; share state across servers
topics.demand_evidence: DesignGurus 'most frequently asked system design questions' (tips: rate limiting)

topics.title: Docker vs VM: what a container really is
topics.hook: VM boots a whole OS vs container starts in moments
topics.catch: Containers share the host kernel, so isolation is weaker
topics.verdict: Containers for packaging and speed; VMs when you need hard isolation
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #14
topics.source_note: Primary/secondary source pages fetched 2026-11-17; every claim traced in specs/T11.json "sources". Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Exponential backoff with jitter
topics.hook: 1,000 clients retry together every second and re-crash the server
topics.catch: Plain retries synchronize into a thundering herd
topics.verdict: Double the wait each time and add randomness
topics.demand_evidence: Nucamp 'Top 25 Backend Interview Questions 2026' #4 (idempotent retries) adjacent

topics.title: Why is Redis so fast? (one thread)
topics.hook: Redis serves every request on a single thread. So, is it slow or fast? Guess now.
topics.catch: One slow command makes every other client wait.
topics.verdict: So Redis is fast because every request is tiny.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: sequel to 'Why is Kafka so fast' (top views); famous name + paradox hook
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Deadlock: two transactions, who wins?
topics.hook: Two transactions each lock one row, then each wants the other's row. Who wins: the first, the second, or nobody?
topics.catch: You can't predict which one gets killed.
topics.verdict: And retry the one that gets aborted.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: sequel to optimistic locking (best retention); conflict + who-wins quiz
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Spot the bug: SQL injection in 3 seconds
topics.hook: This login query has one bug that lets anyone in. You have three seconds. Spot it.
topics.catch: Escaping quotes by hand is not the fix.
topics.verdict: So never build SQL with string glue.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: spot-the-bug quiz format; security stakes like password video (high retention)

topics.title: Git doesn't store diffs
topics.hook: Most developers think Git saves the changes you make. So, diffs or full copies? Pick one.
topics.catch: Change one byte and the hash changes, so history can't be edited unnoticed
topics.verdict: So Git is a database of snapshots, keyed by hash.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: famous tool + myth bust; guess-first
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: ₹100 left your account and never arrived
topics.hook: A hundred rupees leaves your account, the server crashes, and it never arrives. Lost, refunded, or never left?
topics.catch: Crash between the two steps without a transaction, and the money vanishes
topics.verdict: So with a transaction, the money never left.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: money-at-stake story like optimistic locking; 3-option quiz
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Node.js: one thread, so many users
topics.hook: Node.js runs your JavaScript on one thread. So how does it serve so many users? Guess.
topics.catch: One slow callback blocks everyone.
topics.verdict: So keep each callback small, and move heavy work off the loop.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: famous name + paradox like Kafka
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Café Wi-Fi vs your password (HTTPS/TLS)
topics.hook: You log in on café Wi-Fi. Can a stranger on the same network read your password? Yes or no?
topics.catch: HTTPS only protects the trip. Once it arrives, storing it safely is the site's job.
topics.verdict: So check for HTTPS before you type.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: personal-security stakes like password video; yes/no quiz

topics.title: HashMap: 1 key in a million, 1 step
topics.hook: Find one key among a million in a Java HashMap. Does it check a million items, twenty, or one? Guess.
topics.catch: That only works if the hashes spread out.
topics.verdict: So write a good hash code for your keys.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: guess-the-number quiz; classic interview question

topics.title: You press Enter: how many round trips?
topics.hook: You type a site and press Enter. How many round trips before your browser can even ask for the page? Guess.
topics.catch: Every round trip costs time, so a far away server feels slow before it sends a single byte.
topics.verdict: That's why nearby servers matter so much.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: classic interview question, framed as a count-the-steps quiz
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Round robin vs least connections: which server?
topics.hook: Server A is busy with slow requests, and server B is idle. With round robin, where does the next request go? Guess.
topics.catch: Neither one helps if a server is dead
topics.verdict: So use least connections when requests vary, and keep health checks on.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: A-or-B quiz; classic system design question
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Your app crashes at 3 AM: who restarts it?
topics.hook: Your app crashes at three in the morning. Who restarts it before anyone wakes up? Guess.
topics.catch: A restart doesn't fix a bug: back-off grows 10, 20, 40 s, capped at 5 min (CrashLoopBackOff)
topics.verdict: So restarts buy you time, not a fix.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: famous name + relatable 3 AM stakes
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: n² vs n log n at a million items
topics.hook: Sorting a million items. One algorithm takes n squared steps, another takes n log n. How big is the gap? Guess.
topics.catch: With ten items, the gap is tiny, so either is fine.
topics.verdict: So check the growth, not the speed on your laptop.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: guess-the-gap quiz; interview staple
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: Why far-away sites feel slow: CDN
topics.hook: Your server is in Mumbai, and a user in New York opens your site. Why is it slower for them? Guess.
topics.catch: Copies can go stale. Each one lives for its TTL, set in the HTTP header.
topics.verdict: So cache what rarely changes, and set the TTL on purpose.
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: relatable location hook (Mumbai user base)
topics.source_note: Sources fetched 2026-11-24; claims traced in specs/<ID>.json sources. Owner reviews facts before publishing.

topics.title: How search finds one word: inverted index
topics.hook: A billion documents, and search finds the word you typed almost instantly. Does it read every document? Guess.
topics.catch: Every new document has to be added to the index first.
topics.verdict: Writes cost extra work; that's the price of fast searches
topics.demand_evidence: own analytics 24 Nov: paradox hook (a billion docs, instant)

topics.title: Logs vs metrics vs traces
topics.hook: Site is slow: which tool tells you why?
topics.catch: More telemetry costs money and noise

topics.title: API versioning without breaking clients
topics.hook: Rename one field and every mobile app breaks
topics.catch: Many versions mean many things to maintain
topics.verdict: Version explicitly, deprecate with a date, never remove silently
